A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ScienceBoard environment and benchmark. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent and human evaluations in Tables 3–4, interface comparisons, and appendix stability, difficulty, and failure analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and adds results for UI-TARS-1.5-7B and GUI-Actor-7B.

M1.justification: The ScienceBoard environment, unified action space, state-based evaluation, and planner–grounder procedure are unchanged. The added models are evaluated comparators, not revisions to the proposed framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 169-task benchmark across six domains and retain the same interface, interactive theorem-proving, and cross-application scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds UI-TARS-1.5-7B under screenshot observations. Table 4 adds GUI-Actor-7B as a grounding model paired with GPT-4o. All previously evaluated comparators remain.

E3.justification: The additions use existing screenshot and planner–grounder evaluation settings. No task splits, metrics, observation conditions, or shared execution settings are revised; Appendices C.2–C.3 retain the same prompting, decoding parameters, and execution procedure.

E4.justification: Section 6 extends its analysis of separating planning and grounding with another grounding component, GUI-Actor-7B, while holding the GPT-4o planner fixed. Interface, stability, difficulty, and failure analyses are otherwise unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix B.6 and Figure 7 retain the same three-independent-run stability analysis and error bars. The added table rows introduce no new uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or run-count disclosures.

E6.justification: Table 3 newly reports UI-TARS-1.5-7B at 5.46% overall. In Table 4's four-domain comparison, GPT-4o with GUI-Actor-7B reports 20.44%, exceeding the previously highest entry, GPT-4o with Qwen2.5-VL-72B at 16.96%. Existing numerical results and plotted findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same POMDP definition and trajectory equation. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same environment and benchmark contributions and the claim that current agents fall substantially short of reliable scientific assistance.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning grounding, domain knowledge, observation modalities, and modular agents are retained. The limitations concerning binary success evaluation and partial credit, along with the appendix failure explanations, are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds technical documentation identifying the evaluated GUI-Actor as the 7B Qwen2.5-VL-based version and describing its coordinate-free action head. Existing hardware, prompts, decoding settings, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the GUI-Actor paper as reference 65 and briefly describes its grounding approach in Appendix C.1. Existing cited works and ScienceBoard's broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to the backbone list, a new GUI-Actor description, and small wording updates. The main narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 3–4 each gain a row, and Table 3 adds a GUI-action-model color category and revised caption. Appendix content reflows, including Figure 6 moving from page 20 to page 21; existing figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added native GUI-agent evaluation in Table 3 and grounding comparator in Table 4 make the benchmark more informative about specialized GUI systems and broaden support for the planning–grounding analysis. This is a limited empirical improvement: benchmark validation and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, and model-specific implementation details for the additions remain sparse.
